templates.why_chosen: Star-rated: a dashed horizontal divider cleanly separates three data-plane pods above from a two-phase control plane below, with lettered (a)/(b)/(c) callouts tying each crossing arrow to body-text explanation instead of an in-figure legend.
templates.what_to_learn: Use one dashed rule as the entire plane boundary, then letter (not number) the arrows that cross it when their meaning needs the body text rather than a self-contained legend; color the two control-plane phases (orange pre-profiling, green slowdown) so their converging arrows read as one pipeline.

templates.why_chosen: Reassigned from n-panel-comparison by the note-writer: three Pod boxes are simultaneous identical peers in one system, not alternative designs or moments, and the lettered (a)(b)(c) tags label arrow types within one diagram, not separate panels; this is replicated-grid, not n-panel-comparison.
templates.what_to_learn: Reserve lettered (a)(b)(c) tags for distinct panels, not for naming different arrow or relationship types inside one diagram, which just needs a legend instead; draw N simultaneous identical peers (here three pods) as a repeated unit feeding one shared control plane below a dashed divider, replicated-grid's job, not a panel-by-panel comparison.
